tei:note.tei:p: Remaining verses of this poem which are of a mystical character, are

tei:div.tei:p:
The King sustains the earth in justice. He is supreme over all the earth. The whole earth acknowledges and knows, all inhabitants of the world and dwellers on earth, from one end of the earth to the other, that He is Creator of the ends of all the earth who does justice and righteousness on earth. When for justice He rises in court — the earth is silent — to save all the humble of the earth, to make as nought the judges of the earth, to grasp the corners of the earth and throw off all the evil-doers of the earth. Then aloud do they proclaim in heaven and on earth: “How mighty is Thy Name throughout all the earth.” When He rules over all the earth, the depths of the earth shout with joy, the heavens rejoice and the earth exults together with what is in the heavens above the earth and what is in the waters below the earth. Then do they joyfully shout in adoration: “All the earth is full of His glory”. The Lord reigns, the earth rejoices. Three times will He let the Shofar blast be heard in dread and terrify the princes of dwellers on earth, and He will overthrow the thrones of the kingdoms of the earth so that all with breath in their nostrils on earth shall say: “How mighty is Thy Name throughout all the earth.” He establishes joy on the whole earth, arouses all who sleep in the earth, and they will lift up hymns of praise from the corner of the earth: “sing to the Lord, all the earth”.
The earth and its inhabitants await the judgment, they tremble and quake for fear of the judgment, for great is the day of judgment. Who can endure it to justify himself in judgment? All judges and all who know law and judgment and all on whom judgment is to be done, fear lest they will not be favoured in judgment for there is no compassion in judgment. He does not show respect for persons in judgment. He is both witness and plaintiff in judgment, that there may be known on earth His work in judgment. The hand of every man seals the judgment, according to His rule does He perform for him judgment, and according to man’s deeds does He carry out judgment, man’s actions rebuke him in judgment, a stone from the wall cries out in judgment, a wooden beam answers in judgment, everything in truth and everything in judgment with the attribute of compassion and the attribute of judgment. This day is appointed for peoples in judgment, it is assigned as a day of judgment, and on it all souls will He bring to judgment. It has been made a statute in memory of the first day and last day, to remember on it the sleepers of Hebron that in their shadow the lily of Sharon may shelter, those who return to divine protection may be acquitted on it, those who blow the Shofar and cry out aloud in order to profit from the righteousness of their forefathers and be saved through them from anger and wrath. Just as the father (Abraham) kept to the path of justice and clemency, so let kindness and clemency be done in judgment to his descendants. Just as the patient dove (Isaac) sowed clemency, so may his descendants reap truth and clemency. Just as clemency was granted to the one flawless in truth (Jacob) so may there be granted to his descendants truth and clemency. The throne of glory is founded on clemency. In front of Him stands a defender who pleads for clemency, and when the Shofar sounds on behalf of those in need of clemency, then the fathers of clemency entreat and implore and say before Him who loves clemency: “Far be it from Thee who dost speak with clemency, to do justice without clemency, even though in the place of justice there is no clemency and only where there is no justice, is there clemency. But Thou in judgment dost act with clemency to judge the world through acts of clemency, for the foundation of Thy throne is judgment and clemency; and when Thou dost examine deeds lacking in clemency, remember with favour the few deeds done with clemency, and with an unearned gift act with clemency to open for them the treasuries of clemency.”
